brief: Independent interpretation of the same architecture
prompt: Create one original technical concept illustration for a speculative space-transport architecture called SpaceDonkey. Derive the composition independently from the architecture below; do not imitate an infographic layout or any prior image. Show Earth with one continuous structural ring exactly around the equator, centered on Earth and co-rotating with the planet. The ring is the self-supporting compressive backbone of the proposal; do not add an internal orbital rotor, GEO counterweight, Earth-to-space elevator cable, or single giant skyhook. From the ring hang many independent powered swing/tether assemblies inward toward Earth. The swings are intentionally unequal in length, phase, and local role, not evenly repeated decorative pendulums. Show one payload traveling generally eastward and repeatedly entering near-tangent, low-relative-velocity merge corridors with successive swings. At each handoff, electromagnetic guidance aligns the payload, then a mechanical lock carries the load; the payload rides the swing through a finite acceleration arc, receives additional eastward momentum, then is released tangentially into free flight toward another swing. Free-flight legs may rise, coast, glide, or descend; do not depict literal jumping between hooks. The sequence should visibly accumulate sideways/eastward momentum until the final free-flight trajectory becomes orbit around Earth. The important visual distinction is: the equatorial ring remains Earth-fixed/co-rotating, the swings move relative to the ring, and the payload alternates between locked ride phases and free flight. Make the architecture understandable by looking, with the flavor of serious early-2000s transhumanist/futurist proposal art rather than sleek contemporary corporate branding. Schematic, physically minded, richly illustrated, no visible words, labels, numbers, logos, watermarks, or copyrighted characters.
